findings.title: Concurrent builds for the same index key are no longer serialized
findings.body: BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for the entire build; now it only locks around the final map write. Two goroutines can call BuildIndex for the same NamespacedResource at the same time because getOrCreateIndex has no per-key lock and both Search and watch-event handling can call it. For file-backed indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory, which can fail or corrupt the index; for memory indexes they create two separate indexes, the last one wins in the cache, and callers may keep using a different instance. Add a per-key mutex or singleflight and re-check the cache under it before building.

findings.title: TotalDocs ranges over the cache without locking
findings.body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no cacheMu, while BuildIndex now writes to the same map under cacheMu. The new log line in searchSupport.init (resource/search.go:216) calls TotalDocs after starting the watch goroutine, so an event can trigger getOrCreateIndex/BuildIndex and mutate the map while TotalDocs iterates, causing a fatal concurrent map iteration and map write. Hold cacheMu.RLock in TotalDocs and around all cache iterations.

findings.title: init shares one err variable across errgroup workers
findings.body: Each errgroup goroutine assigns to the outer err via `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and also increments totalBatchesIndexed without synchronization. With multiple workers these are data races; one successful build can overwrite another build's error before it is returned, so errgroup.Wait may see nil and startup can continue with a missing index. Use local per-goroutine error variables (`_, _, buildErr := s.build(...); return buildErr`) and an atomic or mutex-protected counter.

findings.title: Watch loop dereferences nil when the event channel is closed
findings.body: The goroutine receives from events without checking the closed-channel ok value, then passes nil to handleEvent, which dereferences evt.Type. The SQL backend closes its WatchWriteEvents channel when the backend is stopped (defer close(stream) in sql/backend.go:572), so stopping a search-enabled server will panic the process. Receive with `v, ok := <-events` and return when !ok, and tie the watcher to a cancelable lifecycle context. The same closed-channel pattern exists in server.initWatcher.

findings.title: Constructor leaks initialized resources when Init fails
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) and returns nil on failure, but never calls s.cancel() or lifecycle.Stop. If lifecycle.Init and search.init succeeded and a later step such as initWatcher fails, the search watch goroutine and open DB resources are left running with a context that is never canceled. Clean up on the error path before returning.

findings.title: Postgres integration test is skipped, hiding startup regressions
findings.body: This PR changes when unified storage is initialized (constructor instead of first RPC) and the only integration test exercising the storage-server target is now skipped for Postgres. That removes CI coverage for exactly the startup path being changed and can hide failures. Fix the test or add equivalent Postgres coverage instead of skipping.
